title: In this town, the number over your head is how many people know your name
premise: In a town where a glowing number over every head counts the people who know your name, my number has said 1 for years, and my brother's has been falling since he began studying alone in the domed reading room where we used to sit together, while a person printed in reverse, with no number at all, takes a table nearer to him every afternoon.
twist: You don't count yourself. My 1 was never me, it was my brother, the only person in town who knew my name, and his last 1 was me, so I was never out of his count: I say both our names once, aloud, in the silent room.
world: A round public reading room under a rain-streaked glass dome with green plaster walls, oak tables and brass-and-green lamps on one closing timer, plus library steps in the sun, a party, a station platform, a wet street and a small flat.
